Use the OpenFOAM solver twoPhaseEulerFoam to simulate a steady-state, incompressible, two-phase oil–water flow in a horizontal pipe with diameter 0.05 m and length 5 m, aligned along the x-direction.
Create a hex-dominant mesh by extruding a single wedge cross-section along the pipe length, with radial refinement near the wall to resolve the boundary layer.
Run the case as a steady-state simulation, iterating until residuals and global mass and phase balances are converged.
Define two incompressible phases in constant/transportProperties: water as the continuous reference phase with density 1000 kg/m³ and kinematic viscosity 1e-6 m²/s, and oil as the second phase with density 800 kg/m³ and kinematic viscosity 1e-5 m²/s.
Set the surface tension coefficient sigma between water and oil to 0.03 N/m.
Use the standard k-epsilon turbulence model with per-phase k and epsilon fields and standard wall functions, since the water-based inlet Reynolds number is approximately 50000.
At the inlet patch, set U to fixedValue uniform (1 0 0), imposing a fixed mixture velocity of 1 m/s in the streamwise direction.
At the inlet patch, set alpha.water to fixedValue uniform 0.3, fixing the inlet water volume fraction at 0.3.
At the inlet patch, set p_rgh to zeroGradient to be consistent with a prescribed velocity inlet.
At the inlet patch, set k to fixedValue uniform 1.5e-3 and epsilon to fixedValue uniform 1.5e-5, which approximates a 5 percent turbulence intensity.
At the outlet patch, set U to zeroGradient, assuming fully developed outflow consistent with the developed-flow goal of the simulation.
At the outlet patch, set alpha.water to zeroGradient, which is the physically correct treatment for an Euler–Euler outflow and explicitly overrides the original requirement that incorrectly specified fixedValue uniform 0.3 at the outlet.
At the outlet patch, set p_rgh to fixedValue uniform 0 to anchor the gauge pressure reference.
At the outlet patch, set k and epsilon to zeroGradient.
On the pipe wall patch, set U to noSlip with value uniform (0 0 0).
On the pipe wall patch, set alpha.water to zeroGradient, enforcing no phase flux through the wall.
On the pipe wall patch, apply standard wall functions for k and epsilon.
Initialize the internal fields with alpha.water uniform 0.3, U uniform (1 0 0), p_rgh uniform 0, k uniform 1.5e-3, and epsilon uniform 1.5e-5.
